definition: Causal AI is a technique in artificial intelligence that builds a causal model and can thereby make inferences using causality rather than just correlation.
details: One practical use for causal AI is for organisations to explain decision-making and the causes for a decision. Systems based on causal AI, by identifying the underlying web of causality for a behaviour or event, provide insights that solely predictive AI models might fail to extract from historical data. An analysis of causality may be used to supplement human decisions in situations where understanding the causes behind an outcome is necessary, such as quantifying the impact of different interventions, policy decisions or performing scenario planning. A 2024 paper from Google DeepMind demonstrated mathematically that "Any agent capable of adapting to a sufficiently large set of distributional shifts must have learned a causal model". The paper offers the interpretation that learning to generalise beyond the original training set requires learning a causal model, concluding that causal AI is necessary for artificial general intelligence.

explainer.lead: Causal AI aims to model why outcomes happen, so it can reason about the effects of actions rather than only spot patterns. That matters when people must explain a decision, compare interventions, or plan policies and scenarios.

tiers.eli5: Imagine noticing that people carry umbrellas whenever the pavement is wet. Umbrellas and wet pavements go together, but umbrellas do not cause the wetness—rain does. Causal AI tries to learn that kind of cause-and-effect story, helping people work out what might happen if they change something.
tiers.practitioner: Use causal AI when the question is what would happen if we changed X, rather than simply what Y is likely to be. Build a causal model of the behaviour or event, then estimate intervention effects or use its causal structure to help explain decisions, potentially alongside a predictive model. A key pitfall is treating predictive accuracy or a strong correlation as evidence that the true causes have been recovered.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation, a causal model represents variables and their cause-effect relationships and supports intervention queries such as P(Y | do(X=x)), rather than relying only on associations such as P(Y | X=x). A 2024 Google DeepMind paper proved that any agent capable of adapting to a sufficiently large set of distributional shifts must have learned a causal model. The authors interpret this as meaning that generalisation beyond the original training set requires causal learning, and conclude that causal AI is necessary for artificial general intelligence; this theoretical result does not mean that predictive correlations alone reveal every underlying cause.

explainer.example: A delivery company notices that late orders often coincide with bad weather. Instead of only predicting which orders will be late, it uses a causal model to estimate whether adding drivers or changing routes would reduce delays, helping it choose an intervention.

usedIn.name: Decision explanation
usedIn.detail: Organisations can use causal models to explain decision-making and identify the causes behind a decision.

usedIn.name: Intervention evaluation
usedIn.detail: Causal analysis can quantify the likely impact of different actions when understanding outcomes is necessary.

usedIn.name: Policy and scenario planning
usedIn.detail: It can supplement human decisions by comparing policy choices and exploring possible scenarios.

explainer.intuition: Predictive AI asks what usually happens together; causal AI asks what produces an outcome and what would change if someone intervened. It represents the underlying web of causes, which can reveal insights that historical patterns alone may not provide.
howItWorks: Define the behaviour, event, or decision that needs explaining.
Build a causal model representing variables and their cause-effect relationships.
Use the model to distinguish causal inference from prediction based only on correlation.
Estimate the effects of interventions or compare alternative policies and scenarios.
Use the resulting insights to supplement human decision-making.
explainer.whyItMatters: Many consequential decisions require more than an accurate forecast: people need to understand causes and compare the effects of possible actions. Causal AI can support that reasoning and make organisational decisions easier to explain.
misconceptions: Causal AI is not simply prediction with a new label; a highly accurate predictive model can still rely on correlations rather than causes.
It does not replace human judgement—the analysis can supplement decisions where understanding causes is necessary.
The DeepMind result is a mathematical claim about adaptive agents, not a demonstration that artificial general intelligence has already been achieved.
